scope: VCFv4.5 local-allele Number=LA/LR/LG and FORMAT fields LAA/LAD/LADF/LADR/LEC/LGL/LGP/LPL/LPP; includes table VCF5.6.

LAA.meaning: Distinct 1-based indices into ALT identifying the alleles relevant to the current sample.

number_definitions.LA: Identical to Number=A except only ALT alleles defined in LAA are considered present.
number_definitions.LR: Identical to Number=R except only ALT alleles defined in LAA are considered present.
number_definitions.LG: Identical to Number=G except only ALT alleles defined in LAA are considered present.

normative_and_recommended_rules.rule: If any local-allele field is present, LAA must also be present and precede all fields other than GT.

LAA is a list of distinct integers giving 1-based ALT indices; it defines which alleles are in play and their interpretation order; LAA is required when interpreting local-allele fields and must be present if any local-allele fields are neither omitted nor MISSING.
Because BCF encodes zero-length vectors as MISSING, a MISSING LAA is treated as an empty vector (REF-only site) if any local-allele fields are neither omitted nor MISSING.

Specification-defined A/R/G FORMAT fields have local equivalents interpreted like their matching global field, except for the ALT alleles considered present and the order in which they are interpreted.
GQ remains genotype quality even when GT is given against local alleles.

Implementation-defined Number=LA local-allele fields should not be used when distinguishing zero-length data from missing data is required at REF-only sites, because BCF encodes empty vectors as missing.
VCF libraries are recommended to expose an API that abstracts local-allele encoding from consumers and accesses values through corresponding non-local keys.

example.finding: Shows local and global field representations encoding the same information across multiallelic records; it is an informative example, not a standalone obligation.
